question.worked_solution:
Remember that the square root of a perfect square can be simplified using absolute value.

$$
\sqrt{{x}^{2}}=|x|
$$

Also, we notice that ${a}^{2}$ and ${b}^{2}$ are perfect squares.

First, we write the expression under the square root as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{a}^{2}{b}^{2}} & =\sqrt{a\cdot a\cdot b\cdot b} \\  & =\sqrt{a\cdot b\cdot a\cdot b} \\  & =\sqrt{(ab)\cdot (ab)} \\  & =\sqrt{(ab)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the absolute value of the squared quantity:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{(ab)^{2}} & =|ab|\end{aligned}
$$
